figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. In vitro biochemical assays of BthII1284 and BthII1282.
(A) Reactions catalyzed by BthII1284 and BthII1282. (B)
Examination of the production of 3 by LC-HRMS. For extracted
ion chromatograms (EICs), the ESI m/z [M + H]+ mode for 3 is
300.0939. Based on the reaction mixture containing 2, Gly, and
BthII1284 (top trace), reactions were conducted in the absence of 2,
Gly, and BthII1284 and with the addition of EDTA, FeSO4, ZnCl2,
MnCl2, MgCl2, and CaCl2, respectively. (C) Examination of the
production of 4 by LC-HRMS. Based on the above reaction mixture
for 3 production, reaction was conducted with the addition of
BthII1282. For EICs, the ESI m/z [M + H]+ mode for 3 is 300.0939,
and the ESI m/z [M −H]−mode for 4 is 164.0214. A 10 ppm mass
error tolerance was used for each trace.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Detection of potential intermediates by LC-HRMS. (A) Time-course analysis of the spontaneous transformation of 5 into 3 utilizing Gly
and 2,2-D2-Gly. For EICs, the ESI m/z [M + H]+ mode for 5, 6, and 3 is 304.1252, 302.1095, and 300.0939, respectively. (B) Time-course analysis
of the spontaneous transformation of 8 into 7 utilizing D-Ala. For EICs, the ESI m/z [M + H]+ mode for 8 and 7 is 362.1306 and 314.1095,
respectively. A 10 ppm mass error tolerance was used for each trace.
